readings.title: The Sabbath Regulations
readings.subtitle: Rest on the Seventh Day
readings.text: [Exodus 35:1] And Mosheh assembled <dn>את</dn> all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, and said to them, “These are the Words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded you to do: [2] “Work is done for six days, but on the seventh day it shall be set-apart to you, a Sabbath of rest to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Anyone doing work on it is put to death. [3] “Do not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”

readings.title: The Freewill Offering
readings.subtitle: Contributions for the Dwelling Place
readings.text: [Exodus 35:4] And Mosheh spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, saying, [5] <dq>‘Take from among you a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Everyone whose heart so moves him, let him bring it as a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: gold, and silver, and bronze,</dq> [6] <dq>and blue, and purple, and scarlet material, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,</dq> [7] <dq>and ram skins dyed red, and fine leather, and acacia wood,</dq> [8] <dq>and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,</dq> [9] <dq>and shoham stones, and stones to be set in the shoulder garment and in the breastplate.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And let all the wise-hearted among you come and make <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded:</dq> [11] <dq><dn>את</dn> the Dwelling Place, <dn>את</dn> its tent and <dn>את</dn> its covering, <dn>את</dn> its hooks and <dn>את</dn> its boards, <dn>את</dn> its bars, <dn>את</dn> its columns, and <dn>את</dn> its sockets,</dq> [12] <dq><dn>את</dn> the ark and <dn>את</dn> its poles, <dn>את</dn> the lid of atonement and <dn>את</dn> the veil of the covering,</dq> [13] <dq><dn>את</dn> the table and <dn>את</dn> its poles, and <dn>את</dn> all its utensils, and <dn>את</dn> the showbread,</dq> [14] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the lampstand for the light, and <dn>את</dn> its utensils, and <dn>את</dn> its lamps, and <dn>את</dn> the oil for the light,</dq> [15] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the incense slaughter-place, and <dn>את</dn> its poles, and <dn>את</dn> the anointing oil, and <dn>את</dn> the sweet incense, and <dn>את</dn> the covering for the door at the entrance of the Dwelling Place,</dq> [16] <dq><dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of ascending offering with <dn>את</dn> its bronze grating, <dn>את</dn> its poles, and <dn>את</dn> all its utensils, <dn>את</dn> the basin and <dn>את</dn> its stand,</dq> [17] <dq><dn>את</dn> the screens of the courtyard, <dn>את</dn> its columns, and <dn>את</dn> their sockets, and <dn>את</dn> the covering for the gate of the courtyard,</dq> [18] <dq><dn>את</dn> the pegs of the Dwelling Place, and <dn>את</dn> the pegs of the courtyard, and <dn>את</dn> their cords,</dq> [19] <dq><dn>את</dn> the woven garments to do service in the set-apart place, <dn>את</dn> the set-apart garments for Aharon the priest and <dn>את</dn> the garments of his sons to serve as priests.’</dq> ” [20] And all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl withdrew from the presence of Mosheh. [21] And everyone whose heart lifted him up and everyone whose spirit moved him came, and they brought <dn>את</dn> the contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the work of the Tent of Appointment, and for all its service, and for the set-apart garments. [22] And they came, both men and women, all whose hearts moved them, and brought earrings and nose rings, and rings and necklaces, all golden goods, even every one who made a wave offering of gold to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] And every man, with whom was found blue and purple and scarlet material, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, and rams’ skins dyed red, and fine leather, brought them. [24] Everyone who would make a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of silver or bronze, brought it. And everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service, brought it. [25] And all the wise-hearted women spun yarn with their hands, and brought <dn>את</dn> what they had spun, <dn>את</dn> the blue and <dn>את</dn> the purple, <dn>את</dn> the scarlet material, and <dn>את</dn> the fine linen. [26] And all the women whose hearts lifted them up in wisdom spun <dn>את</dn> the goats’ hair. [27] And the rulers brought <dn>את</dn> shoham stones, and <dn>את</dn> the stones to be set in the shoulder garment and in the breastplate, [28] and <dn>את</dn> the spices and <dn>את</dn> the oil for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense. [29] The children of Yisra’ěl brought a voluntary offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all the men and women whose hearts moved them to bring all kinds of work which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by the hand of Mosheh, had commanded to be done. [30] And Mosheh said to the children of Yisra’ěl, “See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has called by name Betsal’ěl son of Uri, son of Ḥur, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, [31] and <dn>He</dn> has filled <dn>את</dn> him with the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn>, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all work, [32] to make designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze, [33] and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving wood, and to work in all workmanship of design. [34] “And <dn>He</dn> has put in his heart the ability to teach, in him and Oholiaḇ son of Aḥisamaḵ, of the tribe of Dan. [35] “<dn>He</dn> has filled them with skill to do all work of the engraver and the designer and embroiderer, in blue and in purple, in scarlet material, and in fine linen, and a weaver, doing any work, and makers of designs. [Exodus 36:1] “And Betsal’ěl and Oholiaḇ, and every wise-hearted man in whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given wisdom and understanding, to know how to do <dn>את</dn> all work for the service of the set-apart place, shall do according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded.” [2] And Mosheh called Betsal’ěl and Oholiaḇ, and every wise-hearted man in whose heart <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given wisdom, everyone whose heart lifted him up, to come and do the work. [3] And they received from Mosheh <dn>את</dn> all the contribution which the children of Yisra’ěl had brought for the work of the service of making the set-apart place. But they still brought to him voluntary offerings every morning, [4] so all the craftsmen who were doing <dn>את</dn> all the work of the set-apart place came, each from the work he was doing, [5] and they spoke to Mosheh, saying, “The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded us to do.” [6] Then Mosheh commanded and they sent this word throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman do any more work for the contribution of the set-apart place.” And the people were withheld from bringing, [7] for what they had was enough for all the work to be done, more than enough.

readings.title: Constructing the Dwelling Place
readings.subtitle: The Curtains, Boards, and Veils
readings.text: [Exodus 36:8] Then all the wise-hearted ones among them who worked on <dn>את</dn> the Dwelling Place made ten curtains woven of fine linen and blue and purple and scarlet material. They made them with keruḇim, the work of a skilled workman. [9] The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits, all the curtains having one measure. [10] And he joined <dn>את</dn> five curtains, one to another; and <dn>את</dn> the other five curtains he joined, one to another. [11] And he made loops of blue on the edge of the end curtain of one set, the same he did on the edge of the end curtain of the other set. [12] Fifty loops he made on one curtain, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the end curtain of the second set; the loops held one curtain to another. [13] And he made fifty hooks of gold, and joined <dn>את</dn> the curtains to each other with the hooks, and the Dwelling Place became one. [14] And he made curtains of goats’ hair for the tent over the Dwelling Place, he made eleven curtains. [15] The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits, the eleven curtains having one measure. [16] And he joined <dn>את</dn> five curtains by themselves and <dn>את</dn> six curtains by themselves. [17] And he made fifty loops on the edge of the end curtain in one set, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain of the second set. [18] And he made fifty bronze hooks to join <dn>את</dn> the tent, to be one. [19] And he made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins, dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that. [20] And for the Dwelling Place he made <dn>את</dn> boards of acacia wood, standing up. [21] The length of each board was ten cubits, and the width of each board a cubit and a half. [22] Each board had two tenons for binding one to another. So he did to all the boards of the Dwelling Place. [23] And he made <dn>את</dn> boards for the Dwelling Place, twenty boards for the south side. [24] And he made forty sockets of silver to go under the twenty boards, and two sockets under each of the boards for its two tenons. [25] And for the other side of the Dwelling Place, for the north side, he made twenty boards, [26] and their forty sockets of silver, two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the other board. [27] And he made six boards for the west side of the Dwelling Place. [28] And he made two boards for the two back corners of the Dwelling Place. [29] And they were double beneath, and similarly they were complete to the top by one ring. So he did to both of them for the two corners. [30] And there were eight boards, and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets, two sockets under each of the boards. [31] And he made bars of acacia wood, five for the boards on one side of the Dwelling Place, [32] and five bars for the boards on the other side of the Dwelling Place, and five bars for the boards of the Dwelling Place at the rear, westward. [33] And he made <dn>את</dn> the middle bar to pass through the boards from one end to the other. [34] And he overlaid <dn>את</dn> the boards with gold, and <dn>את</dn> their rings he made of gold to be holders for the bars, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> the bars with gold. [35] And he made <dn>את</dn> a veil of blue and purple and scarlet material, and fine worked linen. It was made with keruḇim, the work of a skilled workman. [36] And he made four columns of acacia wood for it, and overlaid them with gold, with their hooks of gold. And he cast four sockets of silver for them. [37] And he made a covering for the Tent door of blue and purple and scarlet material and fine woven linen, made by a weaver, [38] and <dn>את</dn> its five columns with <dn>את</dn> their hooks. And he overlaid their tops and their rings with gold, but their five sockets were of bronze.
